objections.claim: The release boundary remains fail-open outside the `v*` namespace. The custody manifest deliberately permits the controller and publisher GitHub Apps to retain `contents:write`; GitHub's release API therefore lets either installation create a draft or immediately published release and, when `tag_name` does not exist, create that tag at an attacker-selected `target_commitish`. The proposed tag ruleset restricts only `v*`, so a compromised allowed principal can choose a nonmatching tag such as `x-malicious`, upload arbitrary assets, and publish without entering the Eye-local ceremony. Custody drift still passes because the principal and scope are explicitly allowed; disabling Actions and suspending installations only during the legitimate ceremony does not constrain this out-of-band operation; the release-integrity sweep detects it only after public exposure. Require server-side Eye-only creation/update/deletion protection over every tag namespace that can back a release (for example an all-tags ruleset), or otherwise remove release mutation capability from the machine principals, and add a regression proving a listed controller/publisher credential cannot create or publish a release under an arbitrary non-`v*` tag. Until then blocker 6's publish-allowlist and fail-closed signed-release contract remain unresolved at `fc0fa05`.
